# AuthPolicy

AuthPolicy is a Ziti auth policy: it says with which methods the identities it is assigned to may authenticate, and which second factor they need.

| | |
|---|---|
| API version | `ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Namespaced |
| In Ziti | auth policy, `/edge/management/v1/auth-policies` |
| Updated with | `PUT`: a setting that is left out of the spec is reset to the default of Ziti |

## Example

From [`examples/authpolicy/authpolicy.yaml`](../../examples/authpolicy/authpolicy.yaml):

```yaml
# Identities with this policy authenticate with a certificate and a one-time
# password. Methods that are left out are not allowed.
apiVersion: ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: AuthPolicy
metadata:
  name: certificates-and-totp
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    kind: ProviderConfig
    name: default
  forProvider:
    name: certificates-and-totp
    primary:
      cert:
        allowed: true
        allowExpiredCerts: false
    secondary:
      requireTotp: true
    tags:
      team: platform
```

More manifests of the kind: [`examples/authpolicy/jwt.yaml`](../../examples/authpolicy/jwt.yaml).

## Settings: `spec.forProvider`

| Field | Type | Default | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|------|---------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | string, required |  | `name` | Name of the auth policy. |
| `primary` | object |  | `primary` | Primary authentication methods. A method that is not set is not allowed. |
| `primary.cert` | object |  | `primary.cert` | Cert-based authentication. |
| `primary.cert.allowExpiredCerts` | boolean |  | `primary.cert.allowExpiredCerts` | AllowExpiredCerts allows expired certificates. |
| `primary.cert.allowed` | boolean |  | `primary.cert.allowed` | Allowed enables cert authentication. |
| `primary.extJwt` | object |  | `primary.extJwt` | External JWT authentication. |
| `primary.extJwt.allowed` | boolean |  | `primary.extJwt.allowed` | Allowed enables external JWT authentication. |
| `primary.extJwt.allowedSigners` | list of strings |  | `primary.extJwt.allowedSigners`, as IDs | AllowedSigners is the list of names or IDs of the external JWT signers whose tokens are accepted. Every signer is accepted if it is empty. |
| `primary.updb` | object |  | `primary.updb` | Password (UPDB) authentication. |
| `primary.updb.allowed` | boolean |  | `primary.updb.allowed` | Allowed enables password authentication. |
| `primary.updb.lockoutDurationMinutes` | integer | `0` | `primary.updb.lockoutDurationMinutes` | LockoutDurationMinutes is the duration of a lockout in minutes. Zero locks the identity until an administrator unlocks it. |
| `primary.updb.maxAttempts` | integer | `5` | `primary.updb.maxAttempts` | MaxAttempts is the number of failed logins before lockout. |
| `primary.updb.minPasswordLength` | integer | `5` | `primary.updb.minPasswordLength` | MinPasswordLength is the minimum password length. |
| `primary.updb.requireMixedCase` | boolean |  | `primary.updb.requireMixedCase` | RequireMixedCase requires passwords to have upper and lower case letters. |
| `primary.updb.requireNumberChar` | boolean |  | `primary.updb.requireNumberChar` | RequireNumberChar requires passwords to have a digit. |
| `primary.updb.requireSpecialChar` | boolean |  | `primary.updb.requireSpecialChar` | RequireSpecialChar requires passwords to have a special character. |
| `secondary` | object |  | `secondary` | Secondary authentication factors. |
| `secondary.requireExtJwtSigner` | string |  | `secondary.requireExtJwtSigner`, as an ID | RequireExtJWTSigner is the name or ID of an external JWT signer whose token is required in addition to the primary method. |
| `secondary.requireTotp` | boolean |  | `secondary.requireTotp` | RequireTOTP requires a time-based one-time password. |
| `tags` | map of strings |  | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

The settings every managed resource has, such as `spec.providerConfigRef`,
`spec.managementPolicies` and `spec.writeConnectionSecretToRef`, are described
in [Concepts](../concepts.md).

## How it behaves

- A method that is left out of `primary` is not allowed. Ziti wants all three methods described, and the provider sends them all.
- An auth policy is replaced with `PUT`, because a `PATCH` ignores some of the password settings. A setting that is left out of the spec is reset to the default of Ziti.
- `primary.extJwt.allowedSigners` and `secondary.requireExtJwtSigner` take names or IDs of [`ExternalJWTSigner`](externaljwtsigner.md) resources. An empty list of allowed signers allows every signer.
- Assign the policy to identities with `authPolicyId` of the identity kinds.
- When a signer the policy names is deleted in Ziti, the provider puts the new ID of the signer into the policy once the signer exists again.

## When something goes wrong

- `no entity named "..." in external-jwt-signers` in `Synced`: a signer the policy names does not exist yet.
- Deleting the policy is refused by Ziti and reported in `Synced`: identities or signers still refer to it. Assign them another policy first.
- Identities are locked out after the change: a policy that allows no method they have leaves them unable to sign in. Keep an administrator under the default policy.

Create, update, drift, deletion in Ziti and deletion of the resource are covered by the end-to-end test, see [Testing](../testing.md).
